messages:
jordan: Heads up — noticed a weird interleaving in staging: ExternalSecret annotation ttl seems to cause secrets to flip back to older values after rotation. example: stg-db-creds rotated at 15:03 but ~10s later reverted. @kai @mira any ideas?

kai: Hmm, that sounds like a race between the operator and some other reconciler. Which ExternalSecrets operator/version? And can you paste the ExternalSecret yaml + the k8s secret lifecycle logs?

mira: Also did we just merge the TF change that adjusted any externalsecret annotations? I vaguely remember a PR that set a short ttl for staging.

jordan: Dumping minimal bits: 
```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: stg-db-creds
  annotations:
    external-secrets.io/ttl: "30s"
spec:
  refreshInterval: 30s
  target:
    name: stg-db-creds
```
And k8s events show: secret updated at 15:03:21, updated again 15:03:31 with older value.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] rollout started: externalsecrets-operator v0.7.1 -> v0.8.0 (initiated by mira)

kai: Two likely issues: 1) TTL/refreshInterval shorter than external secret lease/rotation causing operator to fetch stale cached value; 2) two actors (operator + a sync job) both writing the same secret. Do we run vault-sync or another sync at the same time?

sam: We still have vault-sync v1.2 in staging (only reads from Vault and writes k8s secrets for legacy services). It SHOULD be scoped to legacy/* paths, but worth checking. jordan, can you grep controller logs for writes to stg-db-creds?

jordan: quick grep shows two writers around the timestamps: externalsecrets-operator and vault-sync-job-xx. Logs: 
```
externalsecrets-operator: reconciled ExternalSecret/stg-db-creds -> wrote secret version v3
vault-sync-job-xx: wrote secret stg-db-creds -> version v2 (timestamp slightly later)
```
So vault-sync wrote an older version after the operator wrote a newer one.

mira: OK that matches my memory — the TF change (PR #487) changed externalsecret TTL to 30s to speed rotations for onboarding tests. That unintentionally put operator refresh ahead of vault-sync's rotation pipeline. I think we have both systems enabled in staging for testing.

kai: Short-term workaround: bump ExternalSecret annotation to something > vault-sync interval (e.g., 300s) or pause vault-sync writes for that secret. Longer-term: ensure a single writer per secret or add a write lock annotation. We have a pattern: external-secrets.io/managed-by: <owner> or external-secrets.io/lock: "true" to avoid dual writers.

sam: I can quickly patch vault-sync to ignore paths matching staging/managed-by-operator for a day. But better if we change TF in staging to 300s. mira can you open a tiny TF rollback/override PR?

mira: On it — creating PR to set annotation to "300s" for staging and add a comment in the module docs. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/PR-501 (will request sam for review).

ops-bot: [ci] PR-501 lint ok, plan ok, queued for merge after sam approval

jordan: I'll run a smoke test after the change and watch for flips. Also will create a small probe that records secret versions over 10m.

kai: Thanks — once PR is merged we should see no more reverts. Follow-up: let's add an integration test to prevent TTL < vault-sync interval mismatch (catch via terraform plan guard).

mira: Filed follow-up ticket infra#1298 to add TF guard and document the single-writer pattern. Assigning to kai.

sam: Reviewing PR now. If all good I'll merge and pause vault-sync writes for the affected secret until the change hits.

jordan: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll post results here in ~15m.

ops-bot: [alert] staging-secret-flip-rate normalized (was spiking).
